data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Neither idempotency of the operation nor safety of the operation is what the log must require; the log must enforce idempotent *append* via deduplication keys. The distinction between idempotent and safe is real but moot for the log's survival \u2014 the log's own append operation must be made idempotent by construction (operation IDs), decoupling correctness from operation semantics.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log cannot inspect operation content (encrypted/blind appends), deduplication via IDs fails and the log must fall back on requiring idempotent operations.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the log lacks stable storage for the dedup set (e.g., dedup state lost on crash), deduplication is unreliable and operation-level idempotency becomes necessary.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If operation IDs are not globally unique (collision), the dedup mechanism can wrongly discard distinct operations.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The append-only log faces the at-least-once delivery problem at the transport layer, before any operation semantics are evaluated. A retried writer submits the same append request; the log must detect and discard duplicates. The causal mechanism: writer assigns stable operation ID \u2192 transport retries \u2192 log checks ID against existing entries \u2192 duplicate discarded \u2192 single entry survives \u2192 replay applies operation exactly once. This makes the log's append idempotent regardless of whether the encoded operation is idempotent or safe. The distinction between idempotent and safe operations matters only for operations applied directly without a deduplicating log; with a deduplicating log, the log manufactures idempotency at the boundary.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
